clue.text: Volume one contains note by fellow giving complete change of opinion

indicators.note: the volume-and-one pair holds the note and fellow between its two parts

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards
TE is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A book's first volume carries a footnote by a college fellow announcing that he has entirely changed his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contains' places TEF (note plus fellow) inside VOL + ACE, right after VOL. 'by' simply joins note and fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A volte-face is an about-turn, a complete reversal of stance or policy.

clue.text: Girl abandoned different type of writing

indicators.note: the girl's name is dropped from the start of the longer word, as if left behind

parts.note: diverse means different or varied
Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana

explanation.surface: A young woman has given up one style of writing for another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' removes DI from the front of DIVERSE, leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse is metrical composition, poetry as opposed to prose.

clue.text: Delayed, Giles staggers inside to pass the bill

indicators.note: the jumbled name goes within the word for delayed

parts.note: late means delayed or behind time

indicators.note: to stagger is to totter unsteadily, so the name's letters lurch into a new order

explanation.surface: Giles, running late, totters into the chamber in time to vote a measure through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staggers' turns GILES into EGISL, and 'inside' puts that between the L and ATE of LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To legislate is to make laws, which is what a parliament does when it passes a bill.

clue.text: Ten angels and I produce wild flowers

indicators.note: the given letters are worked up into something new, as a factory would produce goods

explanation.surface: Ten angels and the speaker together bring forth flowers of the hedgerow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produce' rearranges TEN, ANGELS and I into the ten-letter answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is sweetbriar, a wild rose of hedgerows.

clue.text: Sour taste left by a lot of police -it begins to yuck

parts.note: the CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is a body of British police detectives
taken as written

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is wanted, the way a word begins

explanation.surface: A nasty taste lingers after a crowd of police have been and gone, and it makes one say yuck.
explanation.walkthrough: The CID is the detective branch of British police forces. 'begins to' takes the Y that opens 'yuck'; 'left by' joins the definition to the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidity is sharpness or tartness on the tongue, the quality of sourness.

clue.text: Even the others left work to get cover

indicators.note: the letters of the first word are put into an other order, a different arrangement, as with 'other' elsewhere in this puzzle

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: The other members evened things out by walking off the job to find shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the others' reshuffles EVEN into ENVE; then L and OP follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To envelop is to wrap up or enclose completely, to cover over.

clue.text: Amount of heat used will run into the millions

indicators.note: the run goes into the middle of the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for million, as in £5m
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A heating bill that will climb into the millions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts R between THE and M.
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a unit of heat, 100,000 British thermal units, used for billing gas in the UK.

clue.text: The friar's food

explanation.surface: What a monk eats.
explanation.walkthrough: Friar Tuck is the jolly friar of the Robin Hood legend; 'tuck' is British, especially schoolboy, slang for food such as sweets and cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: The first is the merry monk of Robin Hood's outlaw band; the second is slang for snacks, as in a tuck shop.

clue.text: Worship as a god? The first two change places improve the mind

indicators.note: the clue spells out that the opening pair of letters swap round, the first moving behind the second

parts.note: to deify is to treat as a god

explanation.surface: Idolising a deity is presented as a way to better oneself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The first two change places' swaps D and E at the start of DEIFY, giving EDIFY.
explanation.definitionFit: To edify is to instruct and uplift, to build up someone's understanding and morals.

clue.text: More malts are brewed in a whirlpool device

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'More malts are brewed in a whirlpool device (9)': the anagram MORE MALTS and definition 'whirlpool' are clear, but 'device' has no job in any parse and the maelstrom is no device; likely garbled in transcription.
annotationWithheld.clue: More malts are brewed in a whirlpool device

clue.text: Criminal turning back to the soldiers of the queen

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

indicators.note: the word for a convict is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a lag is a convict, especially an old lag

explanation.surface: A convict reforms and returns to serve with Her Majesty's troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning back' makes LAG into GAL, and 'to' attaches it after RE, the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal means royal, befitting a king or queen.

clue.text: Even victims without writing can churn out the abuse

indicators.note: to churn something out is to produce it by stirring the mix, so the letters are stirred into a new order
the writing is removed from the fodder before mixing

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Even victims who cannot write are able to pour out a stream of insults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes MS from EVEN VICTIMS, leaving EVENVICTI, which 'can churn out' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Invective is violent denunciation, harsh and insulting language.

clue.text: All that's necessary when doctor sees Stalin

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered into another order

explanation.surface: A physician examines the Soviet dictator and finds only the basics are required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' is a verb, rearranging SEES STALIN; the physician picture is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Essentials are the indispensable things, the basics one cannot do without.

clue.text: Opening batsman expresses agreement at extra runs

indicators.note: the start of the word batsman is wanted, its first letter

parts.note: yes is the word used to agree

explanation.surface: In cricket the opener nods in approval as the bonus runs are added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening batsman' looks like the cricket opener, but gives only B. In cricket, byes are runs scored when the ball passes the batsman untouched, counted as extras.
explanation.definitionFit: Byes are runs credited without the bat touching the ball, part of a cricket team's extras.

clue.text: After victory, point out America was missing, pursuing revenge

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for victory, as in V-sign

indicators.note: the letter for America is absent from the longer word

parts.note: indicative describes what serves to point out or show something

explanation.surface: Having won, someone points out that America was absent, in a spirit of spite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After victory' sets V first; 'was missing' drops the A from INDICATIVE to leave INDICTIVE. 'point out' stands loosely for the adjective indicative.
explanation.definitionFit: Vindictive means vengeful, set on getting even with someone.

clue.text: Make happy by embracing the fate I broadcast

indicators.note: the two letters of by surround the rearranged letters, holding them as in a hug

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered widely, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone accepts the fortune they have scattered abroad and is made content by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns FATE I into EATIF, and 'embracing' puts it between B and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To beatify is literally to make blessed, the original sense being to render supremely happy.

clue.text: Cold tea in commonplace setting? But it has a connection with drunken revelry

indicators.note: the cold tea sits in the commonplace word, which forms its setting

parts.note: banal means trite or commonplace
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
cha (or char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: Cold tea served in ordinary surroundings hardly sounds like a wild party, yet there is a link.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'setting' together put C + CHA inside BANAL, after its BA. CHA is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A bacchanal is a wild drunken party, named after the rites of Bacchus, the god of wine.

clue.text: Playwright accepts second drama will be one to make an impression

indicators.note: the playwright's name takes in a letter as if receiving it

parts.note: Harold Pinter was the English playwright of The Birthday Party and The Caretaker

indicators.note: the second letter of the word drama is the one picked

explanation.surface: A dramatist agrees that his next play will make a mark on audiences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second drama' looks like a follow-up play but gives only R, the second letter of 'drama'; 'accepts' puts it inside PINTER after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: A printer presses inked type or images onto paper, literally making impressions.

clue.text: Time to do something about one's head as understanding

indicators.note: the verb for doing goes round the letter for one

parts.note: to act is to do something, take action
I is the Roman numeral one
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: A moment to deal with one's leader, presented as a matter of mutual understanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside ACT, giving ACIT; NESS, a headland, means 'head' in place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitness is the quality of being implied rather than spoken, a silent understanding.

clue.text: Mild conservative allowed people inside

indicators.note: the people go within the word for allowed

parts.note: let means allowed or permitted
men are people

explanation.surface: A gentle Tory permitted visitors to come into the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts MEN between the E and T of LET.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement weather is mild and pleasant; a clement person is merciful and lenient.

clue.text: Though out manoeuvred, can start to see the birds

indicators.note: letters that are manoeuvred are moved around into a new position

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word is the one used

explanation.surface: Though outflanked, someone can at last spot the birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvred' turns OUT into TOU; then CAN and the S at the start of 'see' follow. 'Though' only sets up the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Toucans are tropical American birds with huge colourful bills.

clue.text: Small amount of modern heartless music to be transposed

parts.note: mod is short for modern, as in mod cons

indicators.note: music that is transposed is shifted to another key, so the letters shift into another order
the central letter of the word is cut out, as a heart from a body

explanation.surface: Only a little modern soulless music needs moving into another key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle S of MUSIC to leave MUIC, which 'to be transposed' rearranges into ICUM after MOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A modicum is a small quantity, as in a modicum of sense.

clue.text: I'd come round with first lyric proving so tuneful

indicators.note: the letters are turned round into a fresh order
the initial letter of the following word is the one taken

explanation.surface: Someone says they will come back with the opening lyric, which turns out to be catchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first lyric' supplies L, which joins I'D COME as the letters 'round' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodic means pleasing in tune, musical and harmonious.

clue.text: A brave man, he takes leads in romantic opera

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the leading letter of each of the next words is picked out

explanation.surface: In a romantic opera, he takes the lead role as the dashing champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads in' takes R and O from 'romantic opera'; the leading man of an opera is also, aptly, its hero.
explanation.definitionFit: A hero is a man admired for courage and noble deeds.

clue.text: A worn out tree

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A tree that has been worn down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges A WORN.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan, or mountain ash, is a small tree with red berries.

clue.text: Cheated about tail back round first corner — then did it again!

indicators.note: the word for cheated goes round everything else

parts.note: duped means cheated or tricked

indicators.note: the reversed tail goes round the corner's initial
the word tail is read in reverse
only the opening letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Having tricked someone, a man doubles back round the first bend and then repeats the trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TAIL into LIAT; 'round' wraps it around C, giving LICAT; 'about' then sets this inside DUPED, after DUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To duplicate is to repeat or copy, doing the same thing a second time.

clue.text: In the event, lost the university records

indicators.note: the letter for university is lost from the event's name

parts.note: the discus is an event in athletics
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: At the athletics meeting, the university team broke no records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' takes the U out of DISCUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Discs are records, the vinyl kind played on a turntable.

clue.text: Way back a king could be an absolute ruler

indicators.note: the abbreviation for way is read from right to left

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: In days gone by, a king might rule without limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ST into TS, before A and R (Latin rex).
explanation.definitionFit: The tsar was the autocratic emperor of Russia, a ruler of unlimited power.

clue.text: Went bananas about steamship and the paper booth

indicators.note: the scrambled word goes round the ship's letters
going bananas is going crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone went crazy over a steamship and the kiosk selling papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' turns WENT into NEWT, 'about' puts SS inside it after NEW, and AND follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A news-stand is a stall or kiosk selling newspapers and magazines.

clue.text: Articles on other times

indicators.note: other means different, so the letters take a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Pieces written on bygone eras.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other' rearranges TIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Items are individual articles or objects in a list.

clue.text: The leaders left it near emergency rafts in the ship

indicators.note: the leading letters of the following words are taken, one from each

explanation.surface: Captains left the emergency rafts by the vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The leaders' picks the first letters of 'left it near emergency rafts'.
explanation.definitionFit: A liner is a large passenger ship of a shipping line.

clue.text: Has suspicions about Oath olio and Church of England victories

indicators.note: the word for having suspicions goes round the church letters

parts.note: to suss is British slang for working out or suspecting
C is the abbreviation for Catholic

explanation.surface: Someone suspects the Catholics and Anglicans of claiming triumphs.
explanation.walkthrough: SUSS is British slang for figure out. 'about' sets C + CE inside SUSSES, after SU.
explanation.definitionFit: Successes are triumphs, achievements that go well.
